issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse parameter mismatch: The problem statement UML declares a helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) in class Farm; the reference solution implements private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java). The template, however, declares the method without a formal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), effectively removing the Animal parameter. This discrepancy can confuse students: they may implement singFarmSong() expecting to call singFarmSongVerse(animal) (as in the UML/solution) and get compilation errors, or they may need to alter the helper's signature to match their implementation, creating non-obvious friction.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to declare the helper with the Animal parameter to match the UML and solution: change the signature to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and either (a) implement the method body to use animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed(), or (b) leave the body as a TODO but keep the correct parameter. This will align template, UML, and solution and avoid compile-time confusion when students implement singFarmSong().

issues.description: Field visibility mismatch for Farm.animals: The UML and problem instructions describe Farm.animals as a private attribute (animals: List<Animal>) with accompanying getter and setter. The reference solution, however, declares the field as public (public List<Animal> animals;). The template currently lacks a concrete field (contains a TODO). This visibility difference deviates from the encapsulation implied by the UML and the written instructions and may confuse students about intended access patterns and whether to use the getter/setter or access the field directly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the animals field private in the solution (and in the template when adding the field) to follow the UML and encapsulation guidance: change declaration to private List<Animal> animals; keep the public getter and setter. Update internal references in the class as needed to use the private field directly and encourage external code to use the getter/setter.
